analysis:
The PR changes only documentation: docs/architecture/model-autopilot.md and docs/provider/cli-reference.md. No source, wire, or configuration code is in the supplied evidence, so I found no concrete security regression.

What the docs now describe:
- model-autopilot.md line 151 and lines 175-212: selected-model recovery can release an adopted, unheld placement after a hold expires. It evicts only under the victim rules (min_dwell_seconds, no per-model lease, idle time). It never evicts the ordinary selection, pins, held slots, or advertised models a request could reload.
- Recovery is busy as `preload`, waits during a live lease or pause, and is cancelled by an add-on hold (`enterAddonHold`). That is consistent with TB-012/T-059 and A-018, which cover availability and add-on hold behavior.
- Lines 278-297 describe a `Configuration change needs a restart to apply` status for enabled_models drift.
- cli-reference.md around lines 956-962: with the coordinator down, a drain with no unfinished work waits 10 s and then finishes without an acknowledgement. Shutdown waits 15 s per model unload and leaves a stuck native retirement to process exit.
- cli-reference.md around lines 1028-1043: status output now prints recovery and restart-needed messages.

Threat-model relevance:
- None of these changes loosens the prefix-cache posture (T-041), the attestation/authorization path (TB-011, T-053), or the coordinator trust boundary (TB-002).
- The no-acknowledgement drain is justified in the text because disconnect already cancelled accepted work.

Unverified contracts for the next review pass:
- Whether the Swift implementation (`ProviderLoop+SelectedModelPlacementPolicy.swift`, `selectedModelRecoveryVictimWait`, `unloadAllModelsForShutdown`) matches the docs. In particular, adoption release must not evict a model with an in-flight request, and the drain without an acknowledgement must not drop usage settlement.
- The docs say the placement policy is pending owner review, so the final behavior is not settled.
- Status and docs must not expose stable identities (T-058). The status text only names models.
